title: Speed camera expansion paused pending provincial legislation
subtitle: Erb Street West expropriation, Blue Box recycling changes, Wilmot pedestrian crossover, and YouthForce funding request.
overview: Regional Council voted to pause further expansion of automated speed enforcement at 28 school zones and to stop hiring for the program, while keeping existing cameras running {{vote:m4}}. The motion responds to the Premier's announced intention to ban speed cameras. Council also asked staff to report on what ending the program would mean.

Council approved expropriating land for Erb Street West road improvements, including a planned roundabout at Bourdeaux Place in Waterloo {{vote:m5}}. It also asked the province to make producers responsible for recycling from public spaces, places of worship, shelters and similar sites. Separately, Council ended its arrangements with Circular Materials at the end of 2025 and will consider drop-off recycling at the Cambridge and Waterloo sites during 2026 budget talks {{vote:m6}}.

In Wilmot, a pedestrian crossover with flashing lights will be installed at Huron and Milton streets {{vote:m7}}. Council also heard a request to keep YouthForce funding in the 2026 budget, and recognized Carlsberg Canada with the Water Efficiency Excellence Award for major water savings.

decisions.detail: Council halted planned expansion to 28 school zones and further hiring, kept current cameras operating, and asked staff to report on the implications of ending the program.
Council approved expropriating part of one property and a temporary grading easement for Erb Street West road improvements, including a roundabout at Bourdeaux Place in Waterloo.

decisions.item: Blue Box advocacy to the province
decisions.detail: Council asked the province to amend the Blue Box regulation so producers cover recycling from all sources, including public spaces and non-profits, and to explain the estimated $171M in municipal savings.
Council supported draft water quantity policy amendments for the Guelph and Guelph/Eramosa wellhead protection area in the amended Grand River Source Protection Plan.

decisions.item: Circular Materials contract and drop-off recycling
decisions.detail: Council agreed all arrangements with Circular Materials end December 31, 2025, and that recycling at Cambridge and Waterloo drop-off sites, about $300,000 a year, be considered in the 2026 budget.
Council approved a Level 2 Type C pedestrian crossover, with flashing beacons, on Huron Street at Milton Street in Wilmot, in place of the Type D staff first recommended.

debate: On the Wilmot crossover, staff said pedestrian volumes only justified the simpler Type D, but a nearby school and steep grade changes supported the upgrade. Staff said the extra cost was manageable and might be phased.
Staff cautioned that flashing lights will not be planned at all future crosswalks, and that nearby residents sometimes complain about them. Staff said they would monitor community impact.

A delegate from Kinbridge Community Association asked for continued annual funding of $100,000 for YouthForce in the 2026 budget, saying it helps secure federal and other grants. Several councillors who had attended its events spoke in support.

On the brownfields grant, staff said the province is working on a legislative fix and that an alternative under the Municipal Act is more limited in the costs it covers. One councillor noted that applicants waiting on the funding are anxious.

A delegate raised concerns about the signature on a speed camera ticket and speed signs without km/h. The Chair said Council has no authority to review or cancel penalty orders, which are set by provincial law.
